sources.title: U15 / U18 Practice Plan — High Performance Practice 4
sources.use: Supports the stated coaching principle. The setup, alternatives and suggested answers are original experimental coaching synthesis, not source-certified.

replacement.limits: Age adaptation and tactical alternatives await coaching review. Static setup: no skating speed, interception timing or uniquely optimal route has been validated. Positional references are examples, not scored targets.

questions.prompt: Who carries the puck after the described pass?
questions.explanation: The puck is assigned to F2; YOU are the passer in the stated rotation.

questions.prompt: Which two things matter when filling high support?

options.text: A need to follow every pass directly to the net

questions.explanation: Support should replace a useful role without duplicating another player.

questions.prompt: Arrange the stated post-pass support change.

options.text: Reoffer high support behind the continuing attack

questions.explanation: The team-plan assumption is explicit; another system might keep the passer closer to Gold’s net.

questions.prompt: Move YOU into a high-slot support example after the pass.
questions.explanation: This position changes from wall carrier to higher support. Avoid occupying D1’s exact point position.

questions.prompt: If F2 immediately loses the puck to Gold 2, what takes priority in your read?

options.text: Completing the offensive rotation without looking
Treating F2 as the carrier anyway
Whether high support can help the defensive transition

questions.explanation: A possession change can turn high support into useful defensive support.

questions.prompt: Name the space you filled and the option it leaves for F2.
questions.explanation: Describe high slot versus point and a possible return connection; do not treat those areas as interchangeable.

questions.prompt: What should YOU communicate after F2 receives?

options.text: I am high support; tell me if the inside lane changes
The entry guarantees a clean setup
F3 remains low even if the inside lane changes

questions.explanation: The call names the changed carrier and keeps high support conditional on coverage.

questions.prompt: Which two cues decide whether to stay high?
questions.explanation: Carrier control and pressure determine whether the high lane remains useful.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to a high-slot support point separated from F2.
questions.explanation: This point sits shallower than F2 (x=12 vs. F2 at x=19), so it actually functions as high support behind the puck instead of sitting even with or deeper than the carrier. It keeps a diagonal connection to F2 while preserving room for F3.

questions.prompt: Gold 2 wins the puck. What responsibility changes first?
questions.explanation: Confirm Gold possession, then recover toward the dangerous lane. The former entry support job is no longer current.

reasons.issue: Scene-level grammar defect (lesson 4, subject-verb agreement): cues[0] read "YOU is the passer" instead of "YOU are the passer". This is scene text shared by every linked question (scene = scenario minus questions/version, per the hash function), so the fix cascades to all ten contentHashes even though only q1 also repeats the identical defect in its own explanation.
